Test motif enrichment within an explicit peak universe

Source: R/RunMotifEnrichment.R
RunMotifEnrichment.Rd

Use native Signac background matching and motif enrichment with an auditable foreground and population. Sequence scanning remains available directly via Signac::AddMotifs() and does not require this function or a DAR analysis.

Usage

RunMotifEnrichment(
  object,
  features,
  assay = NULL,
  universe = NULL,
  background = NULL,
  n.background = 40000L,
  match.features = c("GC.percent", "sequence.length"),
  seed = 1L,
  p.adjust.method = "BH",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object containing a validated ChromatinAssay and an aligned native Signac Motif object.

features

Unique foreground peak IDs, all present in universe.

assay

Source chromatin assay; defaults to the active assay.

universe

Eligible peak IDs. With NULL, use all source-assay peaks. For DAR-derived foregrounds, explicitly supply the full tested peak universe.

background

Optional explicit population peak IDs, including every foreground peak and contained in universe. With NULL, select reference peaks using native Signac::MatchRegionStats(), then include the foreground in the tested population.

n.background

Maximum number of non-foreground reference peaks selected when matching. If fewer are eligible, all eligible peaks are requested.

match.features

Feature-metadata columns passed to native background matching. Compute verified sequence metadata with Signac::RegionStats().

seed

Random seed for native matching, with the caller's RNG restored.

p.adjust.method

Multiple-testing method passed to Signac::FindMotifs().

verbose

Whether native backends print progress.

Value

A list with the complete native results table and a receipt with exact foreground, eligible universe, tested population, matching parameters, motif IDs and backend versions. The input object is unchanged.

Details

The hypergeometric population includes the foreground, so the foreground is a subset of the tested population. reference in the receipt contains only the matched non-foreground controls; background contains the actual native test population. This differs from passing a numeric background directly to Signac, whose matched list excludes the query. No enrichment formula is reimplemented. All motifs are tested before any downstream display filtering. P-values test one-sided over-enrichment; a fold enrichment below one is not an under-enrichment test. For directional DAR analyses, select up/down foregrounds separately. An enrichment result is a sequence association, not evidence of TF binding. Native undefined fold enrichment for a zero-hit motif is retained, together with its native p-value and multiple-testing result.

See also

RunDEtest()

Examples

if (all(vapply(c("Biostrings", "BSgenome", "TFBSTools", "motifmatchr"),
  requireNamespace, logical(1),
  quietly = TRUE
))) {
  reference <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(chr1 = paste(rep("ACGT", 1200), collapse = "")))
  ranges <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
    seqnames = "chr1", start = seq(1, by = 120, length.out = 40),
    end = seq(100, by = 120, length.out = 40)
  ))
  counts <- Matrix::Matrix(matrix(1, 40, 2,
    dimnames = list(paste0("p", seq_len(40)), c("A", "B"))
  ), sparse = TRUE)
  atac <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = ranges, genome = "toy", verbose = FALSE)
  profile <- matrix(0L, 4, 8, dimnames = list(c("A", "C", "G", "T"), NULL))
  profile[cbind(rep(seq_len(4), 2), seq_len(8))] <- 100L
  pfm <- TFBSTools::PFMatrixList(M1 = TFBSTools::PFMatrix(
    ID = "M1", name = "toy_ACGT", profileMatrix = profile
  ))
  matched <- AddATACMotifs(atac, reference, pfm, genome.id = "toy", verbose = FALSE)
  peaks <- rownames(matched[["peaks"]])
  enrichment <- RunMotifEnrichment(matched, peaks[1:10],
    universe = peaks, background = peaks, verbose = FALSE
  )
  enrichment$results
}
